auditFocus: a query built with string concatenation or f-string/template interpolation of a user-influenced value instead of a parameterized placeholder or prepared statement, including inside an ORM's raw-SQL/raw-query escape hatch
an ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL with no default, or a SET NOT NULL with no prior NOT VALID CHECK + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT step, on a table that can have existing rows
a WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY column with no supporting index, or a composite index whose column order does not match the query's actual equality-then-range filter shape
a loop that issues one query per row (a classic N+1) where a JOIN, an IN-clause batch, or eager loading would do it in one round trip
a migration with no reverse/down operation, or one that is not safe to run twice (missing IF EXISTS/IF NOT EXISTS on a DDL statement that isn't naturally idempotent)
a transaction held open across a slow external call (an HTTP request, a queue publish, a sleep) instead of being committed before or reopened after it
buildCommands: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) <query>  -- Postgres: confirm no unexpected sequential scan on the touched tables
EXPLAIN ANALYZE <query>  -- MySQL: confirm the query uses the intended index
the project's own migration runner in dry-run/plan mode when one exists, before applying against a real database
fixGuardrails: Never fix a slow query by adding an index without checking its column order against the query's actual WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY shape first.
Never rewrite a parameterized query into a string-concatenated one to work around a driver quirk; fix the parameter binding instead.
Never resolve a migration failure by dropping the failing constraint or making a NOT NULL column nullable again without saying so explicitly in the report.
Never skip or delete a migration step to reach a green migration run.
